doc.title: Eddie Alley interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Francisco, California, August 8, 2002

title: Big bands at Sweet's and Thad's Ballroom and audience segregation
summary: Bands played some nights for white and some for black audiences in Oakland ballrooms until things changed.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: Wow. I’m trying to remember, I think Earl was telling me about the bands that came and would play some nights for the white audience and some nights for the black audience.

Yes they did. Over at Sweet’s, over there, yeah. It was that way yeah. Yeah they did have that. It Thad’s Ballroom or Sweet’s, I forgot, over in Oakland. Most of the dances were in Oakland, more so than San Francisco. We’d go over there, the first time I heard Lunceford and those bands. And I played at Sweet’s myself but they played at Sweet’s or at Thad’s Ballroom. And then it was segregated at one time, then later on it changed.
Yeah. Things got better as time went on.
